clue.text: Alibi of former copper's false, finally

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the 's

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word false

explanation.surface: A former policeman's alibi turns out, in the end, to be false.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim offered to clear oneself of blame, a justification or pretext.

clue.text: Top journalist passes on spins

parts.note: ED is the editor, the top journalist
to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A senior journalist dies, and the news spins out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are swirling currents, whirls of water or air, so they are spins.

clue.text: Understood criminal's honest daughter

parts.note: a con is a convict or criminal, plus the 's
true means honest, faithful

explanation.surface: The criminal's daughter was taken to be honest.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe something is to interpret it, so construed means interpreted or taken in a given sense.

clue.text: Weapon is excessive in video game

indicators.note: in puts the excessive word inside the game

parts.note: a sim is a simulation video game
dear means expensive, excessive in price

explanation.surface: A weapon is too much in a violent video game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or other small gun carried at the hip is a handheld weapon.

clue.text: Independent criticised containing nothing special

indicators.note: containing says the word for criticised holds the nothing letter within it

parts.note: slated means harshly criticised
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An independent politician is singled out for criticism, though there's nothing special about them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: an isolated case is a one-off, unlike the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set apart and occurring singly is exceptional, so a one-off case can be called special.

clue.text: Go crazy getting upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Going mad from being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is having an attempt or try, the same idiom as having a shot.

clue.text: Satire of character capturing a politician

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the character word encloses the rest

parts.note: a loon is an eccentric character
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A satirical character takes a politician as its target.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of mocking ridicule of a person, a form of satirical writing.

clue.text: Article cheers Greek character

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A newspaper article salutes a Greek personality.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Attractive person left to embrace woman in tangle

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so the letters enclose the woman

parts.note: a dish is informal for an attractive person
Eve, the first woman

explanation.surface: A good-looking person goes off to hug a woman in a messy situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair or clothes is to make them untidy, to tousle or tangle them.

clue.text: Strip from guy embodying Chippendales' heart

indicators.note: embodying means taking into the body, so the guy word holds the extracted letters

parts.note: a dude is a guy, a fellow

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A man takes his clothes off, inspired by the spirit of the Chippendales male strip troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are a famous male striptease troupe; their twelve-letter name has EN at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to lay bare by removing a covering, a synonym of strip as a verb.

clue.text: Innocuous opening of House missing some members?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: limbs are members of the body, so lacking arms is missing some members; the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: A harmless opening session of the House, with some MPs absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests members of parliament in the House, but here it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocuous means causing no injury or offence, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Section of government ran census for lobby

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the government ran a census, pushing for something in the lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'for lobby' includes the link word 'for'; only 'lobby' swaps for the answer, so the definition is narrowed to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is the hall just inside a building's door, the entrance hall.

clue.text: Containers carrying nearly everything finding waterways

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the containers enclose the rest

parts.note: cans are containers

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Containers holding almost everything turn up in waterways.
explanation.definitionFit: Canals are man-made channels for boats, a kind of waterway.

clue.text: Beer chasing further interminable spirits

indicators.note: chasing means running behind, so the beer word comes after
interminable means without end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: more means further, additional
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Endlessly ordering another beer after the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests strong drink beside 'Beer', but it means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and mood of a person or group, their spirits.

clue.text: 'Abbess' is term describing nun

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the words enclose the answer

explanation.surface: 'Abbess' is the word used for a nun in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a religious order of women is called by this family title, and a nun is one.

clue.text: It's forbidden being mean online, but nasty

indicators.note: nasty, in its sense of twisted and ugly, tells us to jumble these letters

explanation.surface: Being nasty and mean on the internet is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo, too shocking to be spoken of, is forbidden in conversation.

clue.text: Start living swallowing drink before noon

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the living word encloses the rest

parts.note: being means existing, living

indicators.note: before puts the drink ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Starting the day by drinking before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something is its start or outset, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Beat to stir up dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rhythmic beat to get people excited and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip a rival is to surpass or outdo them, to beat them.

clue.text: Long crude hint to change drawers, perhaps

indicators.note: to change says these letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A long, crude hint that someone ought to change their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawers are old-fashioned underpants, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers, an old word for knickers or pants, are one example of garments worn under clothes.

clue.text: Illness is caught off some bugs …

indicators.note: off means taken away from the bugs word

parts.note: crickets are insects, loosely bugs
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An illness is caught from some insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a bone-softening disease caused by lack of vitamin D, an illness.

clue.text: … bug's kept quietly for study

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the insect encloses the quiet letter

parts.note: a bug is an insect, and the 's reads as has
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A bug is kept quietly to be studied, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to study or scrutinise.

clue.text: Playmate runs in buff …

indicators.note: in puts the runs letter inside the buff word

parts.note: a fiend is an enthusiast, a buff
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A playmate runs about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In buff' suggests 'in the buff', naked; buff here is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion one plays with, a pal or chum.

clue.text: Put a stop to hard liquor

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan or rumour is to end it decisively
whisky distilled in Scotland is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: Stopping someone drinking spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to quash or thwart, and the noun is whisky from Scotland.

clue.text: … one gazes lecherously, even rudely initially

definitions.text: one gazes lecherously, even rudely initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Following the naked playmate, a leering watcher stares rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay; the leading ellipsis ties it to the previous clue's naked playmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leers and looks lustfully at others is a lecherous starer.

clue.text: Criminal is consumed by lying, right?

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside the lying word

parts.note: prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: Asking whether a criminal is eaten up by lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict serving time in jail is a criminal behind bars, loosely the same person.

clue.text: Regular taking a pew?

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the regular word takes the A in

parts.note: set means fixed or regular, as in a set routine

explanation.surface: A regular churchgoer sits down in the pews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a pew' is the idiom for sitting down, but 'pew' alone is the definition, the question mark showing a pew is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a long bench in a church, an example of a place to sit.

clue.text: Saved by camouflage rolling in grass

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: rolling, as in rolling back, says the camouflage word runs backwards

parts.note: a veil is a covering that disguises

explanation.surface: A soldier rescued by rolling, camouflaged, into long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a besieged town or a worker is to rescue or free them, so saved fits.

clue.text: Experience again return of Wicked Queen

indicators.note: return of means the following words are read backwards

parts.note: evil means wicked
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Going through the comeback of the Wicked Queen once more, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something a second time, in memory or in fact, is to live it once more.

clue.text: Possibly tick answer in usual spot

indicators.note: in places the answer letter between the two other pieces

parts.note: par is the usual or normal level
a site is a spot, a place

explanation.surface: Possibly ticking an answer in its usual place on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' reads as a mark of approval, but it is the blood-sucking mite, one example, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick lives off a host's blood, making it an example of an organism that feeds on another.

clue.text: Following gutted script got on and performed

indicators.note: following means the got-on word comes after the gutted letters
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: to get on in years is to have aged

explanation.surface: After the script was cut, the actors went on stage and performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged is put on and performed before an audience.
